issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning conflates warning and exception contracts
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass meant for warnings.warn, but the code raises it as a fatal exception, and the test asserts pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning) — cementing the wrong contract. Decide the policy: warn-and-proceed via warnings.warn, or refuse with a properly named Error subclass (ValueError/RuntimeError). The PR description itself asks this question; resolve it before merge.

issues.description: Unreachable break after raise inside the misalignment loop
issues.detail: The break immediately following raise PerformanceWarning(msg) is dead code — raise unwinds the frame. This signals the author was torn between fail-fast and collect-all. State the loop's postcondition (report first offending axis vs aggregate all) and write that; delete the stray break.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size computation uses suspicious max(1, itemsize) and dimensionally questionable advice
issues.detail: np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize) papers over a non-case — numpy itemsize is always >= 1. Either drop the guard or name the real case. Worse, the resulting bytes value is surfaced to the user as a recommended array.chunk-size, but the relation is not linear. Either assert the invariant or state the precondition you are advising.

issues.description: Divisibility check only inspects dw[0]; uniformity invariant unstated
issues.detail: The audit examines only the first chunk per axis and renders a verdict for the whole axis. normalize_chunks can produce uneven tails or heterogeneous interiors. Either state the invariant ('all interior chunks equal; only dw[0] need be checked') in a comment, or check every chunk on the axis.

Python parses this as `not ((nominal % zw) == 0)`, which happens to be the intent — but only by precedence accident. Replace with `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:`. Guard clauses should not require the reader to simulate the parser.

issues.description: Test pins the wrong contract via pytest.raises on a Warning subclass
issues.detail: test_zarr_risky_shards_warns asserts pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning), locking the warn-as-exception bug into the contract. Once the warn-vs-raise policy is fixed, switch to pytest.warns or pytest.raises(ValueError) and rename the test to match its actual postcondition.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously refuses this diff in its current form. The core problem is a category error: PerformanceWarning (a Warning subclass) is raised as a hard exception, with unreachable `break` after the raise and a test that pins the confused semantics via pytest.raises. The PR description openly asks whether raising is correct — that policy must be decided before merge. Secondary issues: safe_chunk_size uses max(1, itemsize) to paper over a non-case and surfaces an arithmetically questionable recommendation, the divisibility check inspects only dw[0] without stating a uniformity invariant, and `not x % y == 0` relies on operator precedence. The algorithmic intent (shard shape as previous_chunks) is sound; the validation block needs to be rewritten as a small pure helper with a stated contract.
